source.slice: single competition CompID='237BA891f9949' cut from the restored DB at curation (comp-scoped tables only; CompIDs are case-sensitive hex)

comp.note: 'F5K NI Round 2', latest NZ F5K comp by CompDate and upload at slicing (DateCreated 3804 vs 3802 for same-day 'F5K NI 2', comp 233DDc0ae8889 — story facts, queried 2026-09-04)

identityDecision.because: The server identifies competitions by CompID (case-sensitive hex), not the Jet Comps.CompNo the pipeline's rule 4 expects. A curation surrogate value 0 stands in for the single-comp consistency check across competition.json identity, entries and scores-raw; the real server key rides identity.CompID and this provenance block verbatim. 0 carries no GS semantics anywhere in the loader.

producer.note: no DBParams table exists in the server slice (comp-scoped tables only), so no product version is available; the Jet corpus pins 6.78

extraction.shape: extract.py shape contract reused verbatim: {'schema': {...}, 'rows': [...]}, 2-space indent, ensure_ascii=False, trailing newline, sorted tables, deterministic row order; hex UTF-16LE transport with exact NULL/empty distinction

omittedColumns.ScoringData.Data6, ScoringData.Data7: extracted all-zero (0.000 on all 55 rows); per-flight slots beyond Data5 are unused — omitted from curation, documented here

redaction.pilotNames: REQUIRED (story): server ScoringData.PilotName carries real pilot names. The WI-1 tool redacted 6 distinct pilots (55 name cells) to deterministic Simpsons pilot-pool names keyed on sha256(CompID|PilotNo) before serialisation; FAI_ID blanked on all 55 rows; no helper names existed (HelperName empty everywhere). The mapping is NOT retained anywhere — it exists only in the tool's memory during a run. Real names live only in the gitignored server DB; curated files carry the redacted names only.
redaction.entriesPilots: entries.json pilots rows carry the redacted names (FirstName/LastName split of the tool's PilotName) so the loader's join and the replay's /register-person have labels; they are fiction, never real names.

derivation.entries: DERIVED from ScoringData distinct pilots (75, 79, 80, 82, 88, 102): PilotNo, PilotStartNo, Team (server decimal 0 -> 0) and OmitFromTeamScore (false) come from the rows; the server has NO CompPilots table, so Retired / IsPilot / Role / DrawFreq are NOT derivable and are honestly absent — no defaults invented. Pilot 88 'never flew' is a data fact (all his rows are zero stubs), NOT a Retired flag.
derivation.scoresRaw: One row per ScoringData row (extract order = the tool's deterministic ORDER BY RoundNo, GroupNo, SeqNo, ReFlightNo, PilotNo). Canonical loader columns (TaskNo, RoundNo, GroupNo, ReFlightNo, PilotNo, SeqNo, Penalty, OriginalRoundNo) map 1:1 (TaskNo constant 6 as the Jet F3K/F5K corpus precedent — task identity lives in the F5KData schedule, never in the numeric column; ReFlightNo all 0; OriginalRoundNo == RoundNo everywhere). Penalty persisted as decimal 0.000; carried as integer 0 (the loader column is Integer; value and arithmetics unaffected). Server payload carried verbatim: Data1..5 (per-flight flight-point slots, cell-verified equal to Flight1..4's FPT), Flight1..4 detail strings BYTE-FAITHFUL (see flightStrings below), the server's own Progressive* standings columns, ResultsToRoundNo, Updated, RawScore and NormalisedScore as persisted.
derivation.decimals: The extract's {'$decimal': '...'} wrappers are unwrapped to plain JSON number tokens that keep the persisted scale as text (617.000, 149.500, 955.400, 0.000 — server numeric(18,3) scale 3 throughout). System.Decimal binding is scale-insensitive on ==; curation keeps the server text for byte-faithfulness.

flightStrings.formats: Three coexisting serialisation formats across the 80 flight strings (67 UPPERCASE 3-letter FNO/FTM/TPT/HVA/HPT/NOF/NFP/LOT/LOP/LLN/LLP/OOF/MOS/HPN/SFY/SFP/FPT, 12 lowercase fno/..., 1 legacy long-key FltNbr/MdlID/FltTim/MinSec/TimPts/HgtVal/HgtPts/NbrFlts/NbrFltsPlty/LdgOut/LdgOutPlty/LateLdg/LateLdgPlty/OutOfFld/MotorReStart/HitPerson/Sfty/SftyPlty/FltPts — that legacy one is the shape the story spec described). All carried verbatim; consumers must parse case-insensitively over both key layouts.
flightStrings.fieldMap: ftm/FltTim = packed minutes-seconds (400 = 4:00, 47 = 47 s; Jet Time1Mins packing); tpt/TimPts = clamped scoring seconds; hva/HgtVal = peak altitude m; hpt/HgtPts = band integral over (hva - round NLH); nof/NbrFlts = launch number WHERE IT MATTERS (task B's single stored flight: 1/2/3 -> nfp 0/-10/-20 cumulative launch cost = SeedF5K Task B lookup; inert elsewhere — A/C/D rows vary 1/0/empty with nfp always 0); lot/LdgOut -> landedInPilotArea flag inverse (witnessed once, -10); oof/OutOfFld -> landedOnField zeroing flag (never true); llp/LateLdgPlty + sfp/SftyPlty + MOS/HPN penalty payloads (all zero); MID/ModelID empty everywhere.

raggedness.shape: 55 rows for a 6-pilot x 10-round nominal comp: 30 scored rows (rounds 1–6, five pilots, two groups) + 25 zero stubs. Two distinct mechanisms:
mechanisms: Pilot 88 NEVER FLEW: his five rows (R1 G2, R2 G2, R3 G2, R4 G1, R5 G2) are zero stubs (Updated=False, no flight data, RawScore/NormalisedScore 0.000) and he has NO rows at all from R6 — GS's own progressive standings ranked him 6 with 0.000 total while he was in the draw, then the R6 standings omit him entirely. Absent R6–R10 without stub rows (the f3k-southern-fling retired-pilot shape, but with zero flown scores).

Rounds 7–10 are UNSCORED placeholder rounds: stub rows exist for the five scored pilots only (Updated=False, Downloaded=False, no flight data, all scores 0.000, ProgressiveRank 0), mirroring f3k-sample-comp's NoTaskSet rounds. GS's results were never recomputed past round 6, so the R6 progressive standings are the comp-final standings the DB holds.
raggedness.groupSizes: R1–R5: G1=3, G2=3 (with 88 in the draw); R6–R10: G1=3, G2=2 (88's group unknown — he is out of the draw). Two groups throughout (story facts); no re-flight rows (ReFlightNo=0, OriginalRoundNo==RoundNo on all 55).

verification.invariant: story-named invariant: every persisted RawScore cell recomputes exactly as the sum of per-flight points, each flight point being time points + the signed band integral of the launch ladder (0.5/m below NLH; 1.0/m to 10 m over; 3.0/m beyond) + flight penalties — cell-exact before the oracle is trusted
notes: TPT clamp for target tasks A/D verified under descending-time <-> descending-target any-order pairing (min(seconds, target)); B/C verified under single per-flight cap 300/240. 80/80.

30 s bonus-suppression guard (5.5.10.4, SeedF5K's conditional): UNWITNESSED — the minimum recorded flight is 40 s, so no flight can exercise it; the class definition keeps the guard because the rule carries it, and this data can neither confirm nor deny GS's implementation.

Launch ladder bands verified against the server's own F5KBonusData rows read as bands over (HgtVal - F5KRefHeight): metres <= -1 -> 0.5/m below; 0 -> 0; 1..10 -> 1.0/m over; >= 11 -> 3.0/m beyond (10 x 1.0 then 3.0/m) — SeedF5K LaunchBands exactly (story: 'matches LaunchBands exactly').

normalisationAndDrops.grid: Stored knobs GroupScoreOption=1 (points basis), GroupScoreDecimals=1, RoundOrTruncate=0: every one of the 30 scored cells equals round-half-up(1000 x RawScore / best-in-(RoundNo,GroupNo), 1 dp) — 30/30 including the tie-bearing groups; 12 scored round-groups total, winners at exactly 1000.000 (three groups carry a tied winner: R1G1 75+80, R5G1 75+80, R5G2 80+102 — all share NS 1000.000).
normalisationAndDrops.drops: DropScoreOption=0 = drop worst individual normalised TASK scores; with TaskNo constant 6 one cell per round, so task-mode and round-mode coincide. Activation counts DISTINCT rounds with RawScore>0 (arithmetic story Drop-worst §3): rounds 1–6 all scored, so at 5 completed rounds exactly Drop1At=5's one drop fires (Drop2At=99 never). Verified against all 30 ProgressiveTotalScore cells: ProgTotal = sum(norms) − worst(norms) from R5 on, no drop at R1–4 — 30/30. Equal-candidate tie-break (latest-equally-bad-first, story §5) never bites: no pilot carries two equal normalised minima.
normalisationAndDrops.percent: ProgressivePercent = 100 x ProgressiveTotalScore / leader's ProgressiveTotalScore at 1 dp half-up, 30/30 (display-only).

oracle.source: server-persisted-progressive (GS's own round-6 standings), cross-checked by independent recompute
oracle.divergencePreview: GS's final Score drops the worst REAL normalised score (its option-0 candidate pool is TaskLastRound-gated = MAX(RoundNo) where Updated='True' = 6, arithmetic story Drop-worst §4), while a faithful 10-round replay hands our engine four zero cells per pilot whose dropCount-1 policy then drops a zero and publishes the full sum (pilot 75: ours 5817.600 vs GS 4928.100). Both drop targets induce the identical placing order (verified at curation), so the placing grain matches; WI-3 owns the triage and any divergences.json entry.

loaderModelGapsForWI3: FixtureModels.cs ScheduleTablesTable carries only F3KTaskByRound (Support/Gliderscore/FixtureModels.cs:53) — competition.json's F5KTaskandRefHeightByRound and F5KDataByRound are loader-invisible; ReplayDriver's per-round task lookup F3KTaskByRound(fixture) (Support/Gliderscore/ReplayDriver.cs:793-795) resolves nothing for F5K rounds. WI-3 must widen the schedule model + task lookup.

CaptureInputs branches on GsCompClass == 'F3K' else duration (ReplayDriver.cs:695-698); identity 'F5K2024' falls into CaptureDurationInputs, which refuses (no Dur family row). WI-3 needs an F5K capture map per GS task code decoding Flight1..4 (packed mmss + HVA) into per-flight flightTime + launchAltitude captures (multi-flight, unlike the duration family's single flight).

ScoresRow (FixtureModels.cs:114-129) has no Flight1..4 / Data1..5 members — the curated JSON carries them but the loader ignores them (file-header convention); WI-3's capture map must read the flight strings, widening ScoresRawFile or reading raw elements.

SyntheticFlightLessSlots (ReplayDriver.cs:186-191) needs a 'f5k-ni-round-2' entry: pilot 88 is absent from rounds 6–10 and prescribe-draw demands every registered competitor in every round (the f3k-southern-fling pilot-89 precedent). His group for those rounds is unknowable from the data (draw rows deleted); any group satisfying minPerGroup 2 is flight-less and cell-0, so the choice is score-neutral — document the choice made.
Triage model reads NbrForTeamScore; this fixture carries the server column name NoForTeamScore (inert under UseTeams=false) — deserialises to null, no action, noted for the record.
Three flight-string serialisation formats (see derivation.flightStrings): WI-3's decoder must parse case-insensitively over both key layouts plus the one legacy long-key flight.
